title: Passive Microwave Radiometry and AI-MIDD in Cardiovascular Research: Evidence, Limitations, and a Translational Framework for Drug Development
content: Passive microwave radiometry (MWR) estimates depth-weighted tissue temperature from naturally emitted microwave signals. Its direct cardiovascular evidence comes almost entirely from carotid studies by one research group using one device family: associations with plaque phenotype, a 250-patient prognostic cohort with coronary disease, and small non-randomised studies in which carotid thermal heterogeneity fell during lipid-lowering therapy. Heart-failure and brown-fat applications remain at feasibility level. An illustrative layered neck calculation assigns approximately 4–5% of the 3.8-GHz signal to the arterial wall under its specified assumptions; this is not a measured sensitivity of any clinical device. Mechanistic attribution requires independent anatomical and biological references. We appraise the evidence against established inflammation biomarkers and propose five validation gates (physics, analytical repeatability, biological specificity, clinical increment and decision impact), supported by physics-constrained modelling that reports non-identifiability rather than over-interpreting the signal.
